rules.note: Relocation candidates that only a run of adjacent relocated data words names are the case labels of a jump table, not functions: a run of two or more words naming code, with a word that names an address decoded inside a body and no word that names an entry (or mostly such words), is a table. The ELF pointer-candidate rule, applied to a PE's relocated words (GCC puts the table in .rdata; a case label is never an entry).

A run of three or more adjacent relocated data words naming code, none an entry, most of whose targets do not follow function fill (int3, nop, zero), is a table of case labels packed inside one routine, even when no walk has decoded the labels: compilers start functions on fill. Complements pe-jump-table-relocs, which needs a label already decoded inside a body.

A code address a relocation or a propagated constant names only as the displacement of a memory operand ([index*scale+disp32], [disp32], moffs) is data the program reads: the jump table behind its function in Visual C++ i386 output. A reference that uses the address as a value (push offset, mov reg, imm32, a pointer in a data table) keeps it a candidate.

The filter and handler words of a structured-exception scope-table record ({level, filter or 0, handler}, Visual C++ 7.0 and later) name blocks of the function that pushed the table: not entries, not evidence of a function.

A block that only its predecessor calls and that starts exactly where the predecessor's body ends (Visual C++ __finally blocks and lock regions) belongs to that function; it is folded into it instead of being a function of its own.

An `ff 25` that resolves to an import slot is a linkage stub only behind alignment fill, a ret, zero fill, the previous stub or at the section start; right after other instructions it is the function's own tail call through the import table.

A block right behind a function (where its body ends) whose address only that function takes as a value is the data a compiler puts behind the code that uses it (a Debug build's run-time-check frame description, a jump table), not a function: it is dropped.

The boundary sweep treats `int3` and no-op instructions as the fill between two functions on an x86 PE: the first instruction after a `ret` and its fill, on a 4-byte boundary, is a candidate function start (the walk's own validity checks still judge it). Compilers lay functions out contiguously on fill, so an unreferenced function behind another one is found from its neighbour.

Four or more adjacent relocated words naming code that all lie between two entries with evidence of their own (a call, a symbol, an accepted pattern, a linkage stub), none such an entry, are the case labels of one function's switch: a label that only those words name is dropped. The stretch-of-one-function form of pe-jump-table-relocs, for tables no walk reached (a GCC table whose labels follow loop-alignment fill).
